messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER — High: GPU serving degradation detected in us-west-2 (queue growth + driver Xid). Pager: https://pager.example/INC-4567 :rotating_light:
kevin: I'm seeing request queue length spike on pool-gpu-prod-7, +3k in last 2m. Latency SLOs breached.
tess: confirmed. 503s and throttling increasing. Any recent driver or kernel rollouts?
maria: No driver rollouts in last 24h. We did a minor runtime push 01:15 UTC but it's traffic-shift safe.
raj: Logs show repeated CUDA/Xid 43 on node gpu-node-27 and OOMs on gpu-node-31. Suspect a driver/runtime instability reducing available GPUs.
kevin: Running quick health checks. `kubectl get pods -n gpu-serving -o wide | egrep "gpu-node-2[7|8|9]|gpu-node-31"`
kevin: `gpu-serving-xyz gpu-node-27 CrashLoopBackOff 0/1`
kevin: `dmesg` on gpu-node-27 shows:
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): PID 11987 Comp CUDA RT API
[  125.123456] oom-killer: Killed process 11987 (python) total-vm:12000000kB, anon-rss:11000000kB
```

kevin: Node 27 is flapping, node 31 is reporting CUDA Xid 31/43 and then OOMs.
tess: Immediate mitigation: 1) Remove nodes 27/31 from rotation (evict pods), 2) increase autoscaler max temporarily, 3) enable model-fallback routing to smaller-cap models in eu-west as soft-fallback to keep customers alive.
maria: I'm removing node 27 from LB now: `kubectl label node gpu-node-27 maintenance=true` and cordon + drain.
maria: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-27`
maria: `kubectl drain gpu-node-27 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
kevin: Evictions started. But autoscaler isn't bringing new nodes up — looks like it hit max cap for the pool. Policy shows maxInstances=50 and we're at 50.
raj: Autoscaler logs: `scale request rejected: quotaExceeded` from cloud provider. We need to raise limits or temporarily reconfigure pools.
kevin: Opening emergency capacity request with cloud infra. @oliver can you escalate quota with infra contacts?
oliver: On it. Pinged cloud AM and created ticket CLOU-7893. Estimated time to raise quota ~20-30m.
support-bot: Customer impact: 12 customers with high request failures (>=10% error rate) on hosted API. Top impacted: acme-analytics, beta-startup, chatflow-ai.
tess: Apply temporary rate limiting per-tenant to reduce tail risk and keep service for majority. Can someone push a per-customer token-bucket throttle?
maria: Pushing throttles now: `python ops/scripts/apply_throttle.py --customers acme-analytics,beta-startup,chatflow-ai --rate 5rps`
maria: Throttles in place. Error rates dropping slightly but still elevated.
kevin: Because autoscaler stuck at max, we should enable a fallback to CPU-based serving for lower-priority customers. Workload will be slower but avoids errors.
raj: Triggering routing policy: `PATCH /config/routes` set priority-fallback for pool-gpu-prod -> pool-cpu-fallback.
raj: Routing change pushed. Non-critical traffic starting to drain to CPU pool. Error rate for critical customers improving.
kevin: Cloud quota increase approved by AM — adding 6 more GPUs, provisioning now.
oliver: New instances incoming, should register in ~6m.
kevin: Meanwhile node 31 still shows kernel stack traces. I've captured memory profile and livelock logs: `gsutil cp /var/log/gpu-runtime/gpu-node-31/* gs://redwood-ops/incident-1938001234/`
tess: Good. Please attach logs to incident ticket INC-4567.
kevin: Restarting GPU driver on node 31 as a last resort before recycle: `systemctl restart nvidia-driver`
kevin: Driver restart caused node to successfully recover Xid bursts stopped, pods stabilized.
maria: Node 27 drain completed; pods rescheduled to new nodes and CPU-fallback.
kevin: New GPUs came up and registered. Pool capacity back to normal and queue draining.
support-bot: Customer impact: error rates back down to <1% for all critical customers. Support team notified via ticketing.
raj: Root cause likely interplay between a memory leak in runtime push + high traffic patterns triggering OOMs and CUDA Xid; autoscaler max prevented quick capacity replacement.
tess: Short-term mitigations we applied: cordon/drain bad nodes, route noncritical traffic to CPU pool, apply per-tenant throttles, request emergency quota, restart driver.
maria: Actions to complete before we close the incident: 1) Collect and upload full driver/kernel logs to S3 2) Capture heap dump from runtime for postmortem 3) Revert risky runtime push to canary only 4) Schedule autoscaler max increase and quota formal request
kevin: I'll own log collection and heap dump. Uploaded paths: `gs://redwood-ops/incident-1938001234/logs.tar.gz` and `gs://redwood-ops/incident-1938001234/heapdump.hprof`
raj: I'll draft the initial incident summary and timeline.
tess: I'll coordinate customer comms with support. @support-bot please prepare status update for affected customers and list mitigations and ETA.
support-bot: Drafted and sent to support-channel for review.
oliver: Next steps: assign postmortem owner, schedule deep-dive with runtime and autoscaler teams, propose an autoscaler change to allow emergency burst above reserved max for 15m windows.
maria: Who can take postmortem owner? I can if needed but will need handoff in 4h.
kevin: I can pair on the postmortem with you. I'll be on the incident till 22:00 UTC then hand off.
tess: OK, kevin will handoff to maria at 22:00 UTC. Add follow-ups: telemetry alert tune, add CUDA Xid detector for early paging, autoscaler policy change.
raj: Incident severity: Sev2. Filing INC-4567 with severity and tagging owners: kevin (oncall), maria (postmortem), raj (timeline), tess (customer comms), oliver (cloud escalation).
kevin: Thanks all. We'll run RCA and share draft in 48h. :thumbsup:
maria: Handoff acknowledged. I'll monitor the remainder of the evening and update the channel if anything changes. :sleepy:
oncall-bot: Incident incident-INC-4567 status updated to RESOLVED by kevin at 1938001520
